text:
ConocoPhillips gained 0.6% today as oil prices steadied after a volatile week driven by Middle East tensions. The stock has climbed 5.8% over two weeks as the gap between world oil prices ($123/barrel) and U.S. oil prices ($103/barrel) has widened—a spread that benefits major producers like ConocoPhillips. News Thursday that U.S.-Iran peace talks were resuming eased supply-disruption fears that had pushed prices higher earlier in the week, explaining both yesterday's sharp 3% drop and today's partial recovery.

The broader backdrop matters: earnings season for large oil producers is underway, and investors are watching closely for guidance on future production and capital spending rather than just current profits. With crude prices still well above $100/barrel globally, the company remains well-positioned, but market sentiment remains cautious about whether high oil prices will persist.
